method: Every item checked against its source question in src/data/questions.json (question, answer, key_points, alt_answers, deck_notes, domain, flags, unit, citations_rfo, citations).

Batch content: Korea (LCS and SOFA), Germany (ABG-75), Grants & Agreements, Source Selection and Protests. Korea and Germany items were read clause by clause against their source answers for invented USFK, LCS, SOFA or ABG-75 offices, forms, thresholds or procedures, and for hedges the answer carries ('confirm with C&P', 'verify locally') that an option must not harden.
The five items the author flagged (Q0065, Q0180, Q0176 and Q0182 truncated sources; Q0154 stale $25M; Q0276 thin source) were re-derived from their answers line by line before any other check.

Every RFO number in every cite checked against src/data/regulations.json (crosswalk, unchanged list, thresholds, verified_on 2026-09-13) and, where the crosswalk did not reach a number, against content/out/regulations_map.json (RFO part pages read off acquisition.gov 14 Sep 2026). No acquisition.gov fetch was needed.

Cite convention for questions whose bank citations are empty compared with the accepted convention in mcq_1 through mcq_5 (framework or governing document plus 'official CORB board answer QXXXX', with the local-verification hedge in the cite line).

Machine checks over the whole file for option count, single correct option, difficulty range, duplicate qids, duplicate option texts, missing 'why', domain match, stem length, emails, personal names and ranks, markdown or HTML, non-ASCII characters, 'all of the above', and every dollar figure traced to its source.

changes.type: accuracy of the correct option (source answer imprecise and internally inconsistent with Q0220)
changes.field: correct option text, correct option why
changes.before: That the contract action increases the scope, period, or maximum value of the order. / why: A protest that the action increases the scope, period or maximum value may be heard regardless of the order's value.
changes.after: That the contract action increases the scope, period, or maximum value of the contract under which the order is issued. / why: A protest that the action increases the scope, period or maximum value of the underlying contract may be heard regardless of the order's value.
changes.reason: Q0154's own answer says the action increases the scope, period or maximum value 'of the order', which is close to meaningless (an order cannot exceed its own maximum) and is not what the ground actually is. The bank states it correctly in the same domain: Q0220's answer and key points say 'a protest of an order is allowed only if the order exceeds the scope, period or maximum value of the contract', citing 10 U.S.C. 3406(f). The correction takes the wording from inside the bank rather than from outside it, and it stops the app from shipping two different formulations of the same rule. No fact was added; the distractors and the cite are unchanged.

changes.before: Simplified procedures for the $2.8 million base period, with each option evaluated separately as MND approves it in its own program year. / why: ... the base period alone cannot be used to bring it under a threshold.
changes.after: Simplified procedures for the base period alone, with each option evaluated separately as MND approves it in its own program year. / why: ... the base period cannot be carved out to bring it under a threshold.
changes.reason: The source question gives an IGE of $14 million for a base period plus four options and states no per-period value. '$2.8 million' was an even-split inference, not a number from the source, and the rule is never to invent a number even inside a wrong option. Removing it does not weaken the distractor: the trap is carving the base period out of a $14 million acquisition, not the figure.

changes.before: DoD Other Transactions Guide; Determination and Findings in support of an OTA
changes.after: DoD Other Transactions Guide; official CORB board answer Q0182 (D&F in support of an OTA: cost, technical and schedule risk)
changes.reason: Q0182's bank citations_rfo and citations are both empty, so the item's own authority is the board answer. 'Determination and Findings in support of an OTA' is the document the question asks about, not a source that can be cited. Every other uncited item in this file, and in mcq_5, names the board answer in the cite line; this one did not. No number was added or changed.

changes.reason: The source question and answer say nothing about the project manager's gender. Minor, but it is a detail the stem added to the source, and the fix costs nothing. Options, whys and cite unchanged.

The source answer is one line: 'Also need to consider the approval requirements for this size...Can't use simplified acquisition, must create source selection plan.' Every clause of the correct option traces to it - simplified acquisition unavailable at this value, a source selection plan required, approval requirements for an action this size to be considered - and the only addition, that those approvals bear on the schedule, answers the source question's own third part ('What is your timeline looking like?') and is hedged with 'confirm those approval levels with C&P'. open_notes_for_the_orchestrator: Option-length tell, corpus-wide and not specific to this file. In mcq_6 the correct option is the longest of the four in 37 of 38 items and averages 1.84 times the mean distractor length. Measured for comparison: mcq_1 69% / 1.58, mcq_2 98% / 2.15, mcq_3 90% / 2.31, mcq_4 78% / 1.81, mcq_5 94% / 1.68, and the 260 items already merged into src/data/mcq.json 82% / 1.84. A candidate who always picks the longest option scores far above chance on the Quiz page and the Boss Board. This file is at the corpus average, so nothing was rewritten here - trimming mcq_6's correct options alone would make it inconsistent with the merged bank and would risk cutting the 'confirm with C&P' hedges out of the Korea items, which are part of why those options run long. The fix belongs at corpus level and should lengthen distractors rather than shorten correct options.

Ten items in this file are built on bank answers whose answer_status is ai-draft (Q0092, Q0100, Q0141, Q0220, K101 through K110, K201, K204, K205, K207, K210 - fourteen Korea items plus four others). Fourteen of those also carry korea-verify-cp and verify-locally, and Q0276, Q0279, Q0280 and Q0281 carry verify-locally. The mcq object shape in CONTRACT.md section 3 has no flags field, so the merge into questions.json must keep each parent question's flags and confidence so the app renders the ai-drafted and verify-locally badges. K207's parent is confidence low; the item is narrow enough for that, but the badge matters.

Q0213's cite keeps 'FAR 15.408' exactly as the bank stores it in citations_rfo. That number is not in the regulations.json crosswalk in either direction, so it could not be confirmed as an RFO destination from local sources, and it was left alone rather than converted (the bank's own legacy citations list for this question is ['FAR 15.405'], which the crosswalk maps to FAR 15.407, so the first of the pair is already converted and the second may be a legacy number carried forward from the study material). Worth a verifier pass on the RFO Part 15 page before merge.

Q0168's cite uses 'DoDGARs (32 CFR chapter I subchapter C)'. regulations.json's own notes caution that 'the DoDGARs have been in transition between 32 CFR Chapter I Subchapter C and 2 CFR; 32 CFR Parts 3, 22 and 37 are listed here at medium confidence and should be confirmed before citing.' The same framing is already in four merged mcq_4 items, so this is a bank-wide currency question rather than an item defect, but a single verifier pass over the DoDGARs cites would settle it for all of them.

Q0185's cite says 'Army Warranting Program v7 para 4.2' because that is what the bank answer's Cite line says. The current policy per docs/AGENT_BRIEF.md and regulations.json is Army Warranting Program Policy v12 (MAR 2026). The cite was not changed, since the rule is to use the question's citations, but the parent answer is carrying a stale policy version.
